title: Giant bacteria could be living in your gut | New Scientist
description: Bacteria that are visible without a microscope are generally found in mangroves and fish, but an analysis of different species from around the world suggests they also reside in the human gut
author: Jo Marchant

title: Rare cancer spread between twins in utero | New Scientist
description: In a very rare case, a fetus developed cancer in the uterus, and these tumour cells spread to her twin sister
author: Alice Klein

title: How El Niño could spark a worldwide food crisis | New Scientist
description: Droughts and flooding brought by El Niño threaten crops around the world, raising the risk of increased prices and famines
author: Alec Luhn

title: Dogs are susceptible to the bouba-kiki effect | New Scientist
description: Just like humans, dogs seem to associate the nonsense word “bouba” with a rounded shape and “kiki” with a spiky shape, suggesting the connection stems from brain mechanisms that are shared between species
author: James Woodford

title: Dinosaur named new species a century after fossil found on Isle of Wight | New Scientist
description: Invictibellatrix amberina, a predator in the megaraptoran group of dinosaurs, lived in what is now Britain 120 million years ago and may have had claws 20 centimetres long
author: Chris Simms

title: Brain training shows promise for short-term depression relief | New Scientist
description: Training that encourages people to alter their brain's activity seems to reduce negative emotions among people with depression, but not in the way researchers expected
author: Sascha Brodsky
